# KhelSutra — Product Overview & Early-User Guide

*What it does today, how to get the best out of it, and where it's going.*
*For field associates and for invited alpha / beta academies, coaches, and players.*

---

## In one line

**KhelSutra turns ordinary badminton video into useful pieces — automatically.** Point a phone or
GoPro at the court, record a session, and KhelSutra finds every rally, stitches a **highlight reel**,
and gives you a **simple summary** (how many rallies, how much real play time). No special hardware,
no editing, no manual scrubbing.

---

## The problem we're solving

Academies and serious players already record a lot of video — and then almost never watch it. Hours
of footage pile up on phones and memory cards because cutting it into useful clips by hand is tedious
and nobody has the time. The good rallies, the moments worth reviewing, stay buried.

And most academy halls run **several courts at once**, so a single recording is a busy, noisy scene.
Ordinary video tools choke on that. **Pulling the real rallies out of that footage — automatically —
is exactly what KhelSutra is built to do.**

---

## Who it's for

- **Coaching academies & coaches** — turn raw session footage into review-ready clips and reels for
  teaching, without an editor.
- **Serious players** — get clips of your own rallies to review, keep, and share.
- Today's focus is **badminton academies in Bengaluru** — that's who we're building with first.

---

## What it does **today**

This is what's working right now, in the private web app invited users can try:

- **Upload a full session or match video** (from a phone on a tripod, or a GoPro). Long videos are fine.
- **Automatic rally detection** — it finds where each rally starts and ends, on its own.
- **Highlight reel** — the rallies stitched into one clip you can watch and share, with a small
  *"Generated by KhelSutra.guru"* mark.
- **A simple summary** — how many rallies were found and how much actual play time there was.
- **Re-use & download** — process once, come back to it, download the reel.

That's the core loop: **record → upload → get back a reel + summary.** No editing skill needed.

---

## How to get the best out of it (capture matters)

KhelSutra works best on a **steady, full-court recording** — the same way a coach would set a camera
to review play. A few simple habits make a big difference to the results:

- **Put the camera behind the court, slightly elevated**, with the **whole court in frame**.
- **Keep it still** — a fixed tripod beats a handheld or panning shot every time.
- **Shoot landscape**, with reasonable lighting.
- **Record the whole session** and upload it as-is — KhelSutra does the cutting.

Footage that fights these habits (shaky handheld, heavy zooming/panning, broadcast-style cuts, very
dark halls) is the **hardest case** and where results suffer most. When in doubt: fixed camera, full
court, don't touch it.

> A one-page capture checklist is provided to academies in the trial.

---

## The part that makes KhelSutra different: **it learns from your videos**

This is the heart of the product, and what sets it apart from a generic "AI clipper":

**Your videos make _your_ tool sharper.** As you and your players run more of your own footage through
KhelSutra — and as coaches confirm or correct what it found — the underlying model gets better at
*your* courts, *your* lighting, *your* players, and the busy multi-court halls that trip up everything
else. It improves with use instead of staying frozen.

That same growing library of real, labelled footage is also what unlocks the **deeper features below** —
which is why early users aren't just customers, they're co-builders. Every session you contribute makes
the next version smarter.

**Your data stays yours.** Using your video to improve the model is **opt-in** — nothing is used to train
anything without your explicit permission. We don't publish anyone's footage. **Sessions involving minors
are never used for model improvement.** The product is built **private and local-first**: your video, your
data, your control.

---

## Where it's going — toward an **AI assistant coach**

Today KhelSutra finds rallies and makes reels. The roadmap — fed by the growing video library above —
turns it into a genuine training companion:

- **Shot detection** — recognising smashes, drops, net shots, serves, and clears within each rally.
- **Deeper per-rally and per-match analysis** — patterns, tendencies, what's working and what isn't.
- **Per-player & per-match history** — track a player's progress over weeks and months, not just one clip.
- **Personalised insights** — an **AI assistant coach** that supports (never replaces) the real coach,
  surfacing what to work on next.
- **More sports** — table tennis next, then other racket/court sports.
- **Your language** — Kannada and Hindi, alongside English.

> **Read this honestly:** the items in this section are the **direction**, not today's buttons. What you
> can use *today* is rally detection + highlight reels + the play-time summary. The deeper analysis arrives
> as the video library grows — which is exactly why your footage and feedback matter so much.

---

## What we're focused on over the next ~4 weeks

1. **Growing the library of real academy footage** — especially busy **multi-court** halls (the hard,
   valuable case). This is the single biggest lever on quality.
2. **Field conversations with academies** — understanding how coaches and players actually work with
   video, and what would make this genuinely useful.
3. **Recording sessions and showing academies their own footage** as reels — *"this is what it looks
   like for you."*
4. **Sharpening multi-court accuracy** and inviting a few more academies into the private trial.

---

## What KhelSutra is **not** (so expectations stay honest)

- It's an **early, invite-only trial** — useful, but still improving; you'll hit rough edges.
- It is **not a line-calling, scoring, or umpiring system** — it finds rallies and highlights.
- **Shot detection and the deeper "AI coach" analytics are on the roadmap, not available today.**
- It is **not a replacement for a coach** — it's a tool that saves coaches time and adds insight.
- Accuracy depends on **capture quality**; messy handheld/broadcast footage is a known weak spot.
- **Pricing isn't set** — we're still learning what's fair; today's invited use is about getting it right.

---

## Quick answers to common questions

**"How accurate is it?"**
Very good on a clean, single-court recording. A busy multi-court hall is harder — and is exactly what
we're improving. The best answer is to *show* a sample reel rather than quote a number.

**"Do I need a special camera or hardware?"**
No. A phone or GoPro on a tripod, behind the court, whole court in frame. We provide a one-page checklist.

**"Is my video private? What happens to it?"**
It's built private and local-first — your video stays yours. We never use anyone's footage to improve the
model without explicit opt-in, we don't publish footage, and **footage involving minors is never used**.

**"Can it tell me the score / who won / call lines?"**
Not today. Today it finds rallies and builds a highlight reel + a play-time summary.

**"Does it work for doubles and tournaments?"**
Yes for finding rallies. Crowded multi-court tournament halls are the hard case we're specifically working on.

**"Will it get better?"**
Yes — that's the whole idea. The more real footage runs through it (with permission) and the more coaches
correct it, the sharper it gets, and the sooner shot detection and deeper analysis arrive.

**"Which sports?"**
Badminton today; table tennis and other racket sports are on the roadmap.

**"When can I use it / how do I join?"**
It's an invite-only private trial. If you're interested, the best next step is to let us record a session
and show you your own court and players as a reel.

---

*KhelSutra · khelsutra.guru · Internal & invited-trial overview, June 2026.*
*Field associates: the conversation script and visit rules live in the separate Field Visit Playbook.*

# KhelSutra — Product Overview & Early-User Guide

*What it does today, how to get the best out of it, and where it's going.*
*For field associates and for invited alpha / beta academies, coaches, and players.*

---

## In one line

**KhelSutra turns ordinary badminton video into useful pieces — automatically.** Put a phone or GoPro
on a tripod behind the court, record a session, and KhelSutra automatically finds the rallies, stitches
a **highlight reel**, and gives you a **simple summary** (how many rallies, how much real play time).
No special hardware, no editing, no manual scrubbing.

---

## The problem we're solving

Academies and serious players already record a lot of video — and then almost never watch it. Hours of
footage pile up on phones and memory cards because cutting it into useful clips by hand is tedious and
nobody has the time. The good rallies, the moments worth reviewing, stay buried.

Most academy halls also run **several courts at once**, so a single recording is a busy, noisy scene
that ordinary video tools choke on. **Pulling the real rallies out of busy, multi-court footage is the
hard problem KhelSutra is built to crack** — it already works very well on clean, single-court
recordings, and the multi-court case is exactly what we're sharpening now.

---

## Who it's for

- **Coaching academies & coaches** — turn raw session footage into review-ready clips and reels for
  teaching, without an editor.
- **Serious players** — get clips of your own rallies to review, keep, and share.
- Today's focus is **badminton academies in Bengaluru** — that's who we're building with first.

---

## What it does **today**

This is what's working right now, in the private web app invited users can try:

- **Upload a full session or match video** (from a phone on a tripod, or a GoPro). Long videos are fine.
- **Automatic rally detection** — it finds the rallies and where they start and end, on its own.
- **Highlight reel** — the rallies stitched into one MP4 you can watch, download, and share, with a small
  *"Generated by Khelsutra.guru"* mark.
- **A simple summary** — how many rallies were found and how much actual play time there was.
- **Re-use & download** — process once, come back to it later, download the reel.

That's the core loop: **record → upload → get back a reel + summary.** No editing skill needed.

> Like any automatic tool, it can occasionally miss a real rally or include one that isn't — telling us
> when that happens is genuinely useful feedback, not a sign it's broken (more on that below).

---

## How to use it (alpha)

1. **We set you up** with access to the private web app (it's invite-only; today the app is in English).
2. **Upload your session video.** Large files upload in pieces and can take a while on Indian uplinks —
   that's normal.
3. **It processes in the background.** You can close the tab and come back later; you don't have to sit
   and watch it.
4. **When it's done**, you get the **highlight reel + summary** to watch and download.
5. **Re-process anytime.** (Re-running the same video replaces its earlier result rather than keeping both.)

---

## How to get the best out of it (capture matters)

KhelSutra works best on a **steady, full-court recording** — the same way a coach would set a camera to
review play. A few simple habits make a big difference to the results:

- **Put the camera behind the court, slightly elevated**, with the **whole court in frame**.
- **Keep it still** — a fixed tripod beats a handheld or panning shot every time.
- **Shoot landscape**, with reasonable lighting.
- **Record the whole session** and upload it as-is — KhelSutra does the cutting.

Footage that fights these habits (shaky handheld, heavy zooming/panning, broadcast-style cuts, very dark
halls) is the **hardest case** and where results suffer most. When in doubt: fixed camera, full court,
don't touch it. *(Your field contact provides a one-page capture checklist at setup.)*

---

## The part that makes KhelSutra different: **it gets sharper from real academy footage**

This is the heart of the product, and what sets it apart from a generic "AI clipper":

**The footage that real academies contribute is what makes KhelSutra better over time** — especially on
the busy multi-court halls that are the hard case. When you choose to share your footage, and when
coaches confirm or correct what it found, that growing, labelled library is what we use to sharpen the
tool. It's designed to improve in new versions as that library grows, rather than stay frozen — which is
why early users aren't just customers, they're co-builders.

**Your data stays yours — and sharing is your choice.** We will **never** use your video to improve the
tool without your **clear, explicit agreement** — it is opt-in, never automatic. **Footage involving
minors is never used to improve the tool and is never published.** We never publish your footage; you
decide what, if anything, you share.

**How your video is handled today (plainly):** to produce your reel, your video is processed securely on
our infrastructure, which today includes a trusted cloud AI step — so it does leave your device for
processing. We don't publish it and we don't train on it without your opt-in. An **on-device option**,
where your footage never leaves your own machine, is on the roadmap.

> **Read this honestly:** today the tool gives you rally detection + reels + summaries. It does **not**
> retrain itself as you use it, and there is no per-person tracking. The "gets sharper over time" above is
> the model we're building toward, powered by contributed footage — not a switch that's already on.

---

## Where it's going — toward an **AI assistant coach**

Today KhelSutra finds rallies and makes reels. The roadmap — fed by the growing video library above —
turns it into a genuine training companion:

- **Shot detection** — recognising smashes, drops, net shots, serves, and clears within each rally.
- **Deeper per-rally and per-match analysis** — patterns, tendencies, what's working and what isn't.
- **Per-match history** — track progress over weeks and months, not just one clip.
- **Coaching insights** — an **AI assistant coach** that supports (never replaces) the real coach,
  surfacing what to work on next.
- **More sports** — table tennis next, then other racket/court sports.
- **Your language** — Kannada and Hindi, alongside English.

> **Read this honestly:** the items in this section are the **direction**, not today's buttons. What you
> can use *today* is rally detection + highlight reels + the play-time summary. The deeper analysis arrives
> as the video library grows — which is exactly why your footage and feedback matter so much.

---

## What feedback helps us most (for alpha users)

You don't need to be technical — just tell us, in your words:

- **When it missed a real rally**, or **grabbed something that wasn't a rally.**
- Whether the **reel is the right length and order** for how you'd actually use it.
- **What numbers or details you wish the summary showed.**
- Your real **capture conditions** — how many courts were running, camera/phone, lighting.
- Anything that would make this **genuinely useful for your academy** (or a reason it wouldn't be).

*(Send feedback however is easiest — your KhelSutra contact will tell you where.)*

---

## What we're focused on over the next ~4 weeks

1. **Growing the library of real academy footage** — especially busy **multi-court** halls (the hard,
   valuable case). This is the single biggest lever on quality.
2. **Field conversations with academies** — understanding how coaches and players actually work with
   video, and what would make this genuinely useful.
3. **Recording sessions and showing academies their own footage** as reels — *"this is what it looks
   like for you."*
4. **Sharpening multi-court accuracy** and inviting a few more academies into the private trial.

---

## What KhelSutra is **not** (so expectations stay honest)

- It's an **early, invite-only trial** — useful, but still improving; you'll hit rough edges.
- It is **not a line-calling, scoring, or umpiring system**, and **not player tracking / identification**.
- **Shot detection and the deeper "AI coach" analytics are on the roadmap, not available today.**
- It is **not a replacement for a coach** — it's a tool that saves coaches time and adds insight.
- **Pricing isn't set** — we're still learning what's fair; today's invited use is about getting it right.

---

## Quick answers to common questions

**"How accurate is it?"**
Very good on a clean, single-court recording. A busy multi-court hall is harder — and is exactly what
we're improving. The best answer is to *show* a sample reel rather than quote a number.

**"Do I need a special camera or hardware?"**
No. A phone or GoPro on a tripod, behind the court, whole court in frame. We provide a one-page checklist.

**"Is my video private? What happens to it?"**
We treat your footage as private: we never publish it, and we never use it to improve the tool without
your explicit opt-in. To make your reel, it's processed securely on our infrastructure (which today
includes a trusted cloud AI step), so it does leave your device for processing; an on-device option is on
the roadmap. **Footage involving minors is never used to improve the tool and is never published.**

**"Can it tell me the score / who won / call lines?"**
Not today. Today it finds rallies and builds a highlight reel + a play-time summary.

**"Does it work for doubles and tournaments?"**
It finds rallies in doubles too. Tournament footage varies: a clean, fixed, full-court recording works
well; crowded multi-court tournament halls are the hard case we're specifically working on.

**"Will it get better?"**
Yes — that's the whole idea. The more real footage runs through it (with permission) and the more coaches
correct it, the sharper future versions get, and the sooner shot detection and deeper analysis arrive.

**"Which sports?"**
Badminton today; table tennis and other racket sports are on the roadmap.

**"When can I use it / how do I join?"**
It's an invite-only private trial. If you're interested, the best next step is to let us record a session
and show you your own court and players as a reel.

---

*KhelSutra · khelsutra.guru · Internal & invited-trial overview, June 2026.*
*Field associates: the role description is in the Field Associate flyer, and the conversation script and
visit rules are in the separate Field Visit Playbook.*

    canvas.setFont("Helvetica", 8)

    canvas.restoreState()

                        title="KhelSutra — Product Overview & Early-User Guide",
                        author="KhelSutra")
doc.build(story, onFirstPage=_footer, onLaterPages=_footer)
print("WROTE", OUT)

### 967. assistant (2026-06-15T15:35:01.302Z)

"""Generate highlight reels for the 5 Boxhill June-12 1080p share videos via the GPU
wasb_hybrid path, and drop them into the Drive 'Highlights' subfolder.

Design notes:
- Input = the 1080p Drive copies (NOT the 4K originals), per owner.
- Segmenter = wasb_hybrid (GPU WASB shuttle detection -> Gemini refine), per "use the GPU".
- Each reel is compiled to a LOCAL staging dir first, then MOVED into Drive — so Drive
  never sees a partial file (the exact problem that started this).
- Resumable: skips a video whose reel already exists in the Drive Highlights folder.
- Per-video try/except: one failure doesn't kill the batch.
"""
import os
import shutil
import sys
import traceback

from backend.config import load_config
from backend.infrastructure.database import Database
from backend.pipeline.segmenters.base import segmenter_registry
from backend.pipeline.stitcher.compiler import VideoCompiler
from backend.results import Failure
from backend.utils.hashing import compute_video_id

DRIVE_DIR = r"G:\My Drive\Sharing\Badminton\Boxhill\June 12 2026"
HILITE_DIR = os.path.join(DRIVE_DIR, "Highlights")
STAGE_DIR = r"C:\Users\avidu\Projects\badminton-highlight-indexer\scratch\boxhill_highlights_stage"
DB_PATH = r"C:\Users\avidu\Projects\badminton-highlight-indexer\output\sports_indexer.db"

VIDEOS = [
    "Adarsh v Avi.MP4",
    "Adarsh v Vasant.MP4",
    "Adarsh v Vasant 2.MP4",
    "All 1 v 1.MP4",
    "Vasant vs [Avi and Adarsh].MP4",
]

os.makedirs(HILITE_DIR, exist_ok=True)
os.makedirs(STAGE_DIR, exist_ok=True)

cfg = load_config()
db = Database(DB_PATH)
seg_cls = segmenter_registry.get("wasb_hybrid")

print(f"[boxhill] {len(VIDEOS)} videos -> wasb_hybrid -> {HILITE_DIR}", flush=True)

for i, name in enumerate(VIDEOS, 1):
    src = os.path.join(DRIVE_DIR, name)
    stem = os.path.splitext(name)[0]
    reel_name = f"{stem} - Highlights.mp4"
    final_path = os.path.join(HILITE_DIR, reel_name)
    print(f"\n[{i}/{len(VIDEOS)}] === {name} ===", flush=True)

    if os.path.exists(final_path) and os.path.getsize(final_path) > 0:
        print(f"  SKIP — reel already exists: {final_path}", flush=True)
        continue
    if not os.path.exists(src):
        print(f"  SKIP — source missing: {src}", flush=True)
        continue

    try:
        vid = compute_video_id(src)
        db.add_video(vid, src, "processed", [])
        print(f"  video_id={vid}  segmenting (wasb_hybrid, GPU)...", flush=True)

        segmenter = seg_cls(db, cfg)
        result = segmenter.process_video(vid, src)
        if isinstance(result, Failure):
            print(f"  FAILED segmentation: {getattr(result, 'message', result)}", flush=True)
            continue

        segs = db.query_play_segments(vid, {})
        pairs = sorted((float(s["start_time"]), float(s["end_time"])) for s in segs)
        print(f"  rallies detected: {len(pairs)}", flush=True)
        if not pairs:
            print("  no rallies -> no reel (skipping)", flush=True)
            continue

        # Compile locally first, then move into Drive (never write a partial to Drive).
        vc = VideoCompiler(STAGE_DIR)
        staged = vc.compile_highlights(src, pairs, reel_name)
        size_mb = os.path.getsize(staged) / (1024 * 1024)
        shutil.move(staged, final_path)
        print(f"  REEL DONE: {final_path}  ({size_mb:.0f} MB, {len(pairs)} rallies)", flush=True)
    except Exception:
        print(f"  ERROR on {name}:\n{traceback.format_exc()}", flush=True)
        continue

print("\n[boxhill] batch complete.", flush=True)

96	    """Shared ``wsl -d <distro> bash -c 'source <conda_sh> && <cmd>'`` invocation.
97	
98	    Lives beside (not on) DetectorRunner: a future Linux-native runner must not
99	    inherit WSL plumbing. Requires ``self.cfg`` with ``distro``, ``conda_sh``
100	    and ``timeout_sec`` attributes (TrackNetConfig and WasbConfig both qualify).
101	    ``timeout_sec == 0`` maps to None = wait forever (configs default 1800s).
102	    """
103	
104	    cfg: Any
105	
106	    def _wsl_bash(self, inner_cmd: str) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess:
107	        full = f"source {self.cfg.conda_sh} && {inner_cmd}"
108	        argv = ["wsl", "-d", self.cfg.distro, "bash", "-c", full]
109	        logger.debug("WSL exec: %s", full)
110	        return subprocess.run(argv, capture_output=True, text=True,
111	                              timeout=(self.cfg.timeout_sec or None))

114	    def _wsl_free_gb(self, wsl_path: str) -> Optional[float]:
115	        """Best-effort free space (GB) on the WSL filesystem holding ``wsl_path``.
116	
117	        Returns None if it can't be determined (never raises). Used as a pre-run
118	        disk guard so a long extraction doesn't fill the disk mid-flight.
119	        """
120	        try:
121	            res = self._wsl_bash(f"df -P -B1 {wsl_tilde_quote(wsl_path)} | awk 'NR==2{{print $4}}'")
122	        except (subprocess.TimeoutExpired, OSError):
123	            return None
124	        try:
125	            return int((res.stdout or "").strip()) / (1024 ** 3)
126	        except (ValueError, AttributeError):
127	            return None
128	
129	    def _wsl_rm_rf(self, wsl_paths: List[str]) -> None:
130	        """Best-effort recursive delete of WSL paths (post-success cleanup; never raises)."""
131	        paths = [p for p in wsl_paths if p]
132	        if not paths:
133	            return
134	        quoted = " ".join(wsl_tilde_quote(p) for p in paths)
135	        try:
136	            self._wsl_bash(f"rm -rf {quoted}")
137	        except (subprocess.TimeoutExpired, OSError) as e:
138	            logger.warning("WSL cache cleanup failed (non-fatal): %s", e)

78	def wsl_tilde_quote(path: str) -> str:
79	    """shlex.quote that still lets bash expand a leading ``~/``.
80	
81	    ``shlex.quote("~/clips/x.mp4")`` single-quotes the whole path, so bash
82	    treats ``~`` literally and ``cp``/``mkdir`` fail with "No such file or
83	    directory" — this broke live WSL staging for the default ``~/clips``
84	    stage dir (found by the 2026-06-11 wasb_hybrid smoke run; the BACKLOG
85	    "shlex-quote breaks ~ expansion" item). Quoting only the part after
86	    ``~/`` keeps expansion AND protects spaces/specials in the remainder.
87	    """
88	    if path == "~":
89	        return path
90	    if path.startswith("~/"):
91	        return "~/" + shlex.quote(path[2:])
92	    return shlex.quote(path)
93

- Realistic ETA: ~2–3 hours for all 5 (GPU WASB + Gemini refine per ~12-min video). I'll ping you as each reel lands.

## 🔧 Root cause fixed in the repo — [PR #177](https://github.com/avidullu/badminton-highlight-indexer/pull/177) (merged)
The wastage came from WSL not being able to read Google Drive paths — WASB staged the file with `cp /mnt/g/…`, which silently failed and produced "0 rallies" that *looked* like a real result. The fix:

- A cheap `test -r` **readability preflight** in the shared WSL mixin, called by both WASB and TrackNet runners **before** any frame extraction. An unreadable source (Drive / UNC / network) now **fails fast with one actionable message**: *"…not readable from WSL … copy the video to a local disk and retry"* — instead of wasting a GPU run.
- Tests added (unreadable → fails before `cp`; readable → proceeds; flaky probe → doesn't block). ruff + mypy + 24/24 detector tests + import-smoke green locally.
- Merged via admin on local-green since CI is down account-wide on a **GitHub billing/minutes outage** (`"job was not started because recent account payments have failed"`) — confirmed it's infra, not code. Worth topping up Actions minutes when convenient so CI gates resume.

So next time a video sits on Drive/UNC, the tool tells you exactly what to do in seconds — no silent multi-video waste. (This batch is unaffected: my driver already localizes each file to a local disk first.)

I'll report back the moment video 1's reel appears.

"""Generate highlight reels for the 5 Boxhill June-12 1080p share videos and drop them

Env:
  BOXHILL_SEG    segmenter (default 'wasb_hybrid'; use 'gemini' for the fast cloud path)
  BOXHILL_FORCE  '1' to regenerate reels even if they already exist (default: skip existing)

Design:
- Input = the 1080p Drive copies (NOT the 4K originals), per owner.
- WSL detectors (wasb/tracknet) can't read Google Drive via /mnt -> localize first;
  Gemini reads via host ffmpeg, which reads Drive fine -> no localize.
- Each reel compiles to a LOCAL staging dir first, then MOVES into Drive (Drive never
  sees a partial).
- LOGGING: root logger at INFO so the segmenter's per-chunk/stage lines are captured.
  A combined '_batch_run.log' (whole run) + a per-video '<stem> - run.log' are written
  INTO the Highlights folder for live tailing + posterity.
- Resumable (skip existing reels) unless BOXHILL_FORCE=1. Per-video try/except.
"""
import logging
import os
import shutil
import sys
import traceback

# Run-as-script bootstrap: put the repo root (parent of scratch/) on sys.path.
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))

from backend.pipeline.segmenters.base import segmenter_registry
from backend.pipeline.stitcher.compiler import VideoCompiler
from backend.results import Failure
from backend.utils.hashing import compute_video_id

DRIVE_DIR = r"G:\My Drive\Sharing\Badminton\Boxhill\June 12 2026"
HILITE_DIR = os.path.join(DRIVE_DIR, "Highlights")
STAGE_DIR = r"C:\Users\avidu\Projects\badminton-highlight-indexer\scratch\boxhill_highlights_stage"
DB_PATH = r"C:\Users\avidu\Projects\badminton-highlight-indexer\output\sports_indexer.db"

VIDEOS = [
    "Adarsh v Avi.MP4",
    "Adarsh v Vasant.MP4",
    "Adarsh v Vasant 2.MP4",
    "All 1 v 1.MP4",
    "Vasant vs [Avi and Adarsh].MP4",
]

os.makedirs(HILITE_DIR, exist_ok=True)
os.makedirs(STAGE_DIR, exist_ok=True)

SEG = os.environ.get("BOXHILL_SEG", "wasb_hybrid")
FORCE = os.environ.get("BOXHILL_FORCE") == "1"
NEEDS_LOCAL = SEG in ("wasb_hybrid", "tracknet_hybrid", "yolo_hybrid")

_FMT = logging.Formatter("%(asctime)s [%(levelname)s] %(name)s: %(message)s", "%H:%M:%S")
logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, handlers=[logging.StreamHandler(sys.stdout)])
for h in logging.getLogger().handlers:
    h.setFormatter(_FMT)
# Combined whole-batch log in the Highlights folder (posterity).
_batch_fh = logging.FileHandler(os.path.join(HILITE_DIR, "_batch_run.log"), mode="w", encoding="utf-8")
_batch_fh.setFormatter(_FMT)
logging.getLogger().addHandler(_batch_fh)
log = logging.getLogger("boxhill")

cfg = load_config()
db = Database(DB_PATH)
seg_cls = segmenter_registry.get(SEG)

log.info("%d videos -> %s (needs_local=%s, force=%s) -> %s",
         len(VIDEOS), SEG, NEEDS_LOCAL, FORCE, HILITE_DIR)

for i, name in enumerate(VIDEOS, 1):
    src = os.path.join(DRIVE_DIR, name)
    stem = os.path.splitext(name)[0]
    reel_name = f"{stem} - Highlights.mp4"
    final_path = os.path.join(HILITE_DIR, reel_name)

    if not FORCE and os.path.exists(final_path) and os.path.getsize(final_path) > 0:
        log.info("[%d/%d] SKIP %s — reel already exists", i, len(VIDEOS), name)
        continue
    if not os.path.exists(src):
        log.info("[%d/%d] SKIP %s — source missing", i, len(VIDEOS), name)
        continue

    # Per-video run.log in the Highlights folder (live tail + posterity).
    run_fh = logging.FileHandler(os.path.join(HILITE_DIR, f"{stem} - run.log"), mode="w", encoding="utf-8")
    run_fh.setFormatter(_FMT)
    logging.getLogger().addHandler(run_fh)
    local_src = None
    try:
        log.info("[%d/%d] === %s ===", i, len(VIDEOS), name)
        if NEEDS_LOCAL:
            local_src = os.path.join(STAGE_DIR, name)
            if not (os.path.exists(local_src) and os.path.getsize(local_src) == os.path.getsize(src)):
                log.info("localizing 1080p source (%.0f MB) from Drive...", os.path.getsize(src) / 1024 / 1024)
                shutil.copy2(src, local_src)
            proc_src = local_src
        else:
            proc_src = src  # Gemini: host ffmpeg reads Drive directly

        vid = compute_video_id(proc_src)
        db.add_video(vid, proc_src, "processed", [])
        log.info("video_id=%s  segmenting (%s)...", vid, SEG)

        segmenter = seg_cls(db, cfg)
        result = segmenter.process_video(vid, proc_src)
        if isinstance(result, Failure):
            log.error("FAILED segmentation: %s", getattr(result, "message", result))
            continue

        segs = db.query_play_segments(vid, {})
        pairs = sorted((float(s["start_time"]), float(s["end_time"])) for s in segs)
        log.info("rallies detected: %d", len(pairs))
        if not pairs:
            log.warning("no rallies -> no reel (skipping)")
            continue

        vc = VideoCompiler(STAGE_DIR)
        staged = vc.compile_highlights(proc_src, pairs, reel_name)
        size_mb = os.path.getsize(staged) / (1024 * 1024)
        shutil.move(staged, final_path)
        log.info("REEL DONE: %s  (%.0f MB, %d rallies)", final_path, size_mb, len(pairs))
    except Exception:
        log.error("ERROR on %s:\n%s", name, traceback.format_exc())
        continue
    finally:
        logging.getLogger().removeHandler(run_fh)
        run_fh.close()
        if local_src and os.path.exists(local_src):
            try:
                os.remove(local_src)
            except OSError:
                pass

log.info("batch complete.")

<result>Done. PR #178 is OPEN against `master`, not merged.

## Summary

**Approach chosen:** Option (a) — stream frames directly from the video into the detector, eliminating the PNG disk round-trip, gated behind a default-OFF config flag.

The bottleneck was `wasb_infer.extract_frames`, which wrote ~46k PNGs for a 12-min 1080p60 clip (cv2 PNG encode + decode-on-read dominates; a real run overran the 1800s timeout and silently produced "0 rallies"). The fast path decodes the staged video on the fly with one forward-only `cv2.VideoCapture` and feeds frames into the detector via a scoped `cv2.imread` shim.

**Why output is preserved exactly:** PNG is lossless, so `cv2.imread(cv2.imwrite_png(frame))` returns the identical uint8 BGR array `cap.read()` produced. The shim only replaces the *source of pixels*; every other line of WASB's `ImageDataset.__getitem__` (affine resize to 512×288, ImageNet normalize, channel order) runs unchanged — the detector sees the same frames, same order, same resolution, and the tensor is byte-for-byte identical to the disk path. The resumable cache, tracker re-run, and CSV writer are shared code.

**Files changed (all absolute under the worktree):**
- `backend/pipeline/detectors/wasb_infer.py` — streaming support in `run()` (optional `frame_loader`/`source_key`, forces `num_workers=0`, `video:&lt;abspath&gt;` cache key); new pure helpers `synthetic_frame_path`, `build_windows`, `SequentialFrameStore` (bounded sliding buffer), the `_streaming_imread_patch` context manager, and `make_video_frame_loader`/`run_video_streaming` + `--stream-video` CLI flag.
- `backend/pipeline/detectors/wasb_runner.py` — default-OFF `stream_video` config; passes `--stream-video` vs `--frames_out_dir`, skips disk guard and frame-cache cleanup when streaming.
- `backend/config/models.py` — `stream_video` field on `WasbIndexConfig`.
- `tests/test_wasb_cache.py`, `tests/test_tracknet_runner.py`, `tests/test_config_wasb.py` — unit tests for the pure helpers, eviction/resume semantics, the imread shim, and runner/config wiring (no torch/GPU/real-video needed).

**Test results (local; GPU/WSL treated as unavailable):** ruff clean, mypy clean on the 3 changed backend files, 58 passed across the touched suites + import smoke. A non-trivial design correction surfaced during testing — the detector's per-window access dips back by `frames_in-1` at each window boundary, so the buffer evicts by `max_seen-(frames_in-1)`, not the naive max index.

    def add_video(self, video_id: str, filepath: str, status: str, validation_results: List[Dict[str, Any]]) -> bool:
        """Register or update a video row WITHOUT touching its child segments.

        Uses UPSERT, not INSERT OR REPLACE: REPLACE deletes the conflicting row, which —
        with foreign_keys ON — cascade-deletes every play_segment/event/candidate_segment.
        That made a status update (e.g. marking 'failed' on re-validation, or 'processed'
        before the segmenter runs) silently destroy prior good results. UPSERT mutates the
        row in place; clearing segments is now an explicit, deliberate operation
        (clear_video_data / prune_segments).
        """
        try:
            with self._connect() as conn:
                conn.cursor().execute(
                    "INSERT INTO videos (id, filepath, status, validation_results) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?) "
                    "ON CONFLICT(id) DO UPDATE SET "
                    "filepath=excluded.filepath, status=excluded.status, "
                    "validation_results=excluded.validation_results",
                    (video_id, filepath, status, json.dumps(validation_results))
                )
                conn.commit()
            return True
        except Exception as e:
            logger.error(f"Failed to add video: {e}")
            return False

    def segment_watermarks(self, video_id: str) -> Tuple[int, int]:
        """Return (max play_segment id, max candidate_segment id) for a video (0 if none).

        Captured before a (re)segmentation so the run's new rows (id > watermark) can be
        told apart from prior rows (id <= watermark), enabling destroy-AFTER-confirm.
        """
        with self._connect() as conn:
            cur = conn.cursor()
            p = cur.execute("SELECT COALESCE(MAX(id), 0) FROM play_segments WHERE video_id = ?",
                            (video_id,)).fetchone()[0]
            c = cur.execute("SELECT COALESCE(MAX(id), 0) FROM candidate_segments WHERE video_id = ?",
                            (video_id,)).fetchone()[0]
            return int(p), int(c)

    def _parse_time(val: Union[int, float, str]) -> float:
        """Normalizes a timestamp value to float seconds.
        Handles: float/int (pass-through), plain numeric strings ("12.4"),
        and colon-separated strings ("MM:SS", "HH:MM:SS", "H:MM:SS.ms").
        This mirrors the parse_time logic used in gemini.py to ensure
        the stitcher can always consume whatever format the indexer produced."""
        if isinstance(val, (int, float)):
            return float(val)
        if isinstance(val, str):
            val = val.strip()
            if ":" in val:
                # Handle MM:SS, HH:MM:SS, etc.
                parts = val.split(":")
                parts.reverse()
                total = 0.0
                for i, p in enumerate(parts):
                    try:
                        total += float(p) * (60 ** i)
                    except ValueError:
                        pass
                return total
            try:
                return float(val)
            except ValueError:
                logger.warning(f"Could not parse timestamp value '{val}' as a number. Defaulting to 0.0.")
                return 0.0

### 1148. assistant (2026-06-15T17:15:34.657Z)

Found it, fixed it, merged it, and verified — your reel is no longer doubled.

## The bug
Your instinct was exactly right. The DB held **37 segments** for *Adarsh v Avi* — two near-identical batches at the same timestamps (one per processing run). Two things combined:

1. **`compile_highlights` stitched its segment list verbatim** — no overlap/dedup. A highlight reel should never replay the same footage, but nothing enforced that. ← the real product defect.
2. **How duplicates got in:** `add_video` is an UPSERT (from the earlier "re-ingest must not destroy prior results" change), so it no longer clears child segments. The API path prunes them via destroy-after-confirm, but my scratch batch driver didn't — so the FORCE re-run *accumulated* both runs' rallies.

## The fix — [PR #180](https://github.com/avidullu/badminton-highlight-indexer/pull/180) (merged)
**`VideoCompiler._merge_overlapping`**: before trimming, it sorts and merges any overlapping/abutting ranges — collapsing exact and near-duplicates and true overlaps, while preserving genuinely distinct (gapped) rallies and dropping degenerate rows. So a reel can never stitch the same rally twice, no matter how the duplicates arrived (re-run accumulation *or* chunk-overlap).

**Tests:** 6 in `test_compiler.py` — unit cases for the merge logic (exact/near dup, unsorted+overlap, distinct-preserved, degenerate-dropped, string timestamps) plus an integration test (5 duplicate segments → 3 per-clip trims). **ruff + mypy clean, full suite 692 passed.** I also fixed my batch driver to reset the DB per run (belt-and-suspenders).

**Verified:** re-ran *Adarsh v Avi* → **17 rallies, 285 MB** (was a doubled 620 MB), DB now 17 rows.

The clean Gemini batch is regenerating **all 5** reels (stale doubled ones deleted first); the de-duplicated *Adarsh v Avi* is already in `…\Highlights\`, and the per-video `run.log`s are streaming there. ETA ~25 min for the rest — I'll ping you when they're all in.

Now I understand both the concurrency hazard and the right delivery approach. Let me build this properly. First, the durable **runner** in `tools/` — local-first generation, atomic copy to Drive, resumable, per-video DB reset, and crucially **never deletes other work**:

### 1162. assistant (2026-06-15T17:22:19.603Z)

"""Batch highlight-reel runner — orchestrates "generate highlights for these videos
into this folder" requests with CLEAN, NON-DESTRUCTIVE, resumable execution.

Why this exists (lessons paid for the hard way):
- **Never delete other work.** Reels + per-video run.logs are written to a LOCAL work dir
  first, then COPIED into the destination (atomically: temp name -> os.replace). The
  destination folder is only ever ADDED to — we never bulk-delete it. (A bulk `rm` of a
  Google-Drive-synced folder once lost finished reels + logs.)
- **Drive-sync safe.** Generating directly inside a Google Drive folder races the sync
  client (deleted files resurrect, partial writes sync). Generate locally; publish once.
- **Idempotent re-runs.** Each video's prior DB segments are cleared before processing
  (add_video is an UPSERT and does NOT clear children), so a re-run never accumulates
  duplicate rallies. Belt-and-suspenders with VideoCompiler's overlap-merge (PR #180).
- **Resumable & concurrency-friendly.** A video whose reel already exists in the
  destination is skipped (unless --force); launching a second request never undoes the
  first's published reels. The Gemini path also isolates its chunk workdir per video
  (PR for output/chunks/<video_id>) so concurrent videos don't collide.

Usage:
  python -m tools.generate_highlights --videos-dir "G:\\...\\June 12 2026" \
      --out "G:\\...\\June 12 2026\\Highlights" --segmenter gemini [--force]
  python -m tools.generate_highlights --video A.MP4 --video B.MP4 --out <dir> ...
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import logging
import os
import shutil
import sys
import traceback
from typing import List, Optional

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))

from backend.config import load_config
from backend.infrastructure.database import Database
from backend.pipeline.segmenters.base import segmenter_registry
from backend.pipeline.stitcher.compiler import VideoCompiler
from backend.results import Failure
from backend.utils.hashing import compute_video_id

logger = logging.getLogger("highlights_runner")

# Detectors that run in WSL can't read Google Drive / UNC via /mnt -> localize first.
_WSL_DETECTORS = {"wasb_hybrid", "tracknet_hybrid", "yolo_hybrid"}
_VIDEO_EXTS = (".mp4", ".MP4", ".mov", ".MOV", ".mkv", ".avi")


def _atomic_publish(local_path: str, dest_path: str) -> None:
    """Copy local_path -> dest_path so the destination never sees a partial file.

    Copy to a temp sibling, then os.replace (atomic on the same volume). Never deletes
    anything else in the destination folder.
    """
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(dest_path), exist_ok=True)
    tmp = dest_path + ".publishing.tmp"
    shutil.copy2(local_path, tmp)
    os.replace(tmp, dest_path)


def generate_highlights_batch(video_paths: List[str], out_dir: str, *, segmenter: str,
                              local_work_dir: str, db_path: str, force: bool = False) -> dict:
    """Generate one highlight reel per input video into out_dir. Returns a summary dict.

    Non-destructive: only ADDS reels/logs to out_dir (atomic publish); never deletes.
    """
    os.makedirs(out_dir, exist_ok=True)
    os.makedirs(local_work_dir, exist_ok=True)
    needs_local = segmenter in _WSL_DETECTORS

    cfg = load_config()
    db = Database(db_path)
    seg_cls = segmenter_registry.get(segmenter)

    # Combined batch log (local; published at the end).
    fmt = logging.Formatter("%(asctime)s [%(levelname)s] %(name)s: %(message)s", "%H:%M:%S")
    if not logging.getLogger().handlers:
        logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, handlers=[logging.StreamHandler(sys.stdout)])
        for h in logging.getLogger().handlers:
            h.setFormatter(fmt)
    batch_log_local = os.path.join(local_work_dir, "_batch_run.log")
    batch_fh = logging.FileHandler(batch_log_local, mode="w", encoding="utf-8")
    batch_fh.setFormatter(fmt)
    logging.getLogger().addHandler(batch_fh)

    summary = {"done": [], "skipped": [], "no_rallies": [], "failed": []}
    logger.info("highlights runner: %d videos -> %s (segmenter=%s, force=%s)",
                len(video_paths), out_dir, segmenter, force)

    for i, src in enumerate(video_paths, 1):
        name = os.path.basename(src)
        stem = os.path.splitext(name)[0]
        reel_name = f"{stem} - Highlights.mp4"
        dest_reel = os.path.join(out_dir, reel_name)
        local_reel = os.path.join(local_work_dir, reel_name)

        if not force and os.path.exists(dest_reel) and os.path.getsize(dest_reel) > 0:
            logger.info("[%d/%d] SKIP %s — reel already published", i, len(video_paths), name)
            summary["skipped"].append(name)
            continue
        if not os.path.exists(src):
            logger.warning("[%d/%d] SKIP %s — source missing", i, len(video_paths), name)
            summary["failed"].append(name)
            continue

        run_log_local = os.path.join(local_work_dir, f"{stem} - run.log")
        run_fh = logging.FileHandler(run_log_local, mode="w", encoding="utf-8")
        run_fh.setFormatter(fmt)
        logging.getLogger().addHandler(run_fh)
        staged_src: Optional[str] = None
        try:
            logger.info("[%d/%d] === %s ===", i, len(video_paths), name)
            if needs_local:
                staged_src = os.path.join(local_work_dir, name)
                if not (os.path.exists(staged_src) and os.path.getsize(staged_src) == os.path.getsize(src)):
                    logger.info("localizing source (%.0f MB)...", os.path.getsize(src) / 1024 / 1024)
                    shutil.copy2(src, staged_src)
                proc_src = staged_src
            else:
                proc_src = src

            vid = compute_video_id(proc_src)
            db.clear_video_data(vid)          # idempotent: no cross-run accumulation
            db.add_video(vid, proc_src, "processed", [])
            logger.info("video_id=%s segmenting (%s)...", vid, segmenter)

            result = seg_cls(db, cfg).process_video(vid, proc_src)
            if isinstance(result, Failure):
                logger.error("segmentation FAILED: %s", getattr(result, "message", result))
                summary["failed"].append(name)
                continue

            segs = db.query_play_segments(vid, {})
            pairs = sorted((float(s["start_time"]), float(s["end_time"])) for s in segs)
            logger.info("rallies detected: %d", len(pairs))
            if not pairs:
                logger.warning("no rallies -> no reel")
                summary["no_rallies"].append(name)
                continue

            # Compile locally, then publish atomically into the destination.
            VideoCompiler(local_work_dir).compile_highlights(proc_src, pairs, reel_name)
            _atomic_publish(local_reel, dest_reel)
            try:
                os.remove(local_reel)
            except OSError:
                pass
            logger.info("PUBLISHED reel: %s (%d rallies)", dest_reel, len(pairs))
            summary["done"].append(name)
        except Exception:
            logger.error("ERROR on %s:\n%s", name, traceback.format_exc())
            summary["failed"].append(name)
        finally:
            logging.getLogger().removeHandler(run_fh)
            run_fh.close()
            # publish this video's run.log (additive; never deletes anything in out_dir)
            try:
                _atomic_publish(run_log_local, os.path.join(out_dir, f"{stem} - run.log"))
            except OSError:
                pass
            if staged_src and os.path.exists(staged_src):
                try:
                    os.remove(staged_src)
                except OSError:
                    pass

    logging.getLogger().removeHandler(batch_fh)
    batch_fh.close()
    try:
        _atomic_publish(batch_log_local, os.path.join(out_dir, "_batch_run.log"))
    except OSError:
        pass
    logger.info("DONE. %s", {k: len(v) for k, v in summary.items()})
    return summary


def _resolve_videos(args) -> List[str]:
    if args.video:
        return [v if os.path.isabs(v) else os.path.join(args.videos_dir or ".", v) for v in args.video]
    if args.videos_dir:
        return sorted(
            os.path.join(args.videos_dir, f) for f in os.listdir(args.videos_dir)
            if f.endswith(_VIDEO_EXTS) and os.path.isfile(os.path.join(args.videos_dir, f))
        )
    raise SystemExit("provide --videos-dir or one/more --video")


def main() -> None:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Batch highlight-reel runner (clean, non-destructive).")
    ap.add_argument("--videos-dir", help="folder of source videos (all videos in it, unless --video given)")
    ap.add_argument("--video", action="append", help="explicit source video (repeatable)")
    ap.add_argument("--out", required=True, help="destination folder for reels + run.logs")
    ap.add_argument("--segmenter", default="gemini", help="segmenter registry key (default: gemini)")
    ap.add_argument("--local-work", default=os.path.join("output", "highlights_work"),
                    help="local staging dir (reels compiled here, then published)")
    ap.add_argument("--db", default=os.path.join("output", "sports_indexer.db"))
    ap.add_argument("--force", action="store_true", help="regenerate even if a reel already exists")
    args = ap.parse_args()
    generate_highlights_batch(_resolve_videos(args), args.out, segmenter=args.segmenter,
                              local_work_dir=args.local_work, db_path=args.db, force=args.force)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""tools/generate_highlights.py — the batch highlight runner. The load-bearing guarantees
are NON-DESTRUCTIVE + atomic publish + idempotent skip; those are what we lock here
(heavy deps — segmenter/compiler/db — are mocked)."""
import os
from unittest.mock import MagicMock, patch

import tools.generate_highlights as gh


def test_atomic_publish_is_nondestructive(tmp_path):
    src = tmp_path / "local_reel.mp4"
    src.write_bytes(b"reel-bytes")
    dest_dir = tmp_path / "out"
    dest_dir.mkdir()
    sibling = dest_dir / "Someone Else - Highlights.mp4"
    sibling.write_bytes(b"do-not-touch")

    gh._atomic_publish(str(src), str(dest_dir / "Me - Highlights.mp4"))

    assert (dest_dir / "Me - Highlights.mp4").read_bytes() == b"reel-bytes"
    assert sibling.read_bytes() == b"do-not-touch"          # sibling untouched
    assert not list(dest_dir.glob("*.publishing.tmp"))      # no partial left behind


def test_resolve_videos_explicit_and_dir(tmp_path):
    (tmp_path / "a.MP4").write_bytes(b"x")
    (tmp_path / "b.mp4").write_bytes(b"x")
    (tmp_path / "notes.txt").write_text("ignore")
    args = MagicMock(video=None, videos_dir=str(tmp_path))
    found = gh._resolve_videos(args)
    assert [os.path.basename(p) for p in found] == ["a.MP4", "b.mp4"]   # videos only, sorted
    args2 = MagicMock(video=["only.MP4"], videos_dir=str(tmp_path))
    assert gh._resolve_videos(args2) == [os.path.join(str(tmp_path), "only.MP4")]


def test_batch_skips_existing_reel_and_preserves_other_work(tmp_path):
    """force=False: a video whose reel already exists is skipped, the segmenter is never
    called, and unrelated files already in the destination are left intact."""
    out = tmp_path / "out"
    out.mkdir()
    (out / "Adarsh v Avi - Highlights.mp4").write_bytes(b"already-published")
    (out / "Adarsh v Avi - run.log").write_text("prior log")
    other = out / "Someone Else - Highlights.mp4"
    other.write_bytes(b"untouched")
    src = tmp_path / "Adarsh v Avi.MP4"
    src.write_bytes(b"src")

    seg_registry = MagicMock()
    with patch.object(gh, "load_config", return_value={}), \
         patch.object(gh, "Database", return_value=MagicMock()), \
         patch.object(gh, "segmenter_registry", seg_registry):
        summary = gh.generate_highlights_batch(
            [str(src)], str(out), segmenter="gemini",
            local_work_dir=str(tmp_path / "work"), db_path=str(tmp_path / "db.sqlite"), force=False)

    assert summary["skipped"] == ["Adarsh v Avi.MP4"]
    seg_registry.get.assert_not_called()                 # never processed
    assert other.read_bytes() == b"untouched"            # other work preserved
    assert (out / "Adarsh v Avi - Highlights.mp4").read_bytes() == b"already-published"

### 1220. assistant (2026-06-15T17:36:31.387Z)

"""Cold-start verifier for the Boxhill highlight regen (task b8ecngf9u via tools/generate_highlights.py).

Confirms each reel is DEDUP-CLEAN — i.e. the "every rally stitched twice" bug (#180) is gone — by
checking, per source video:
  - video_id + DB play_segments count (one run's worth → clear_video_data worked; no accumulation)
  - any near-duplicate / overlapping segment PAIRS in the DB (should be 0; that's what doubling looked like)
  - the published reel exists, size (MB), and the rally count parsed from its `<stem> - run.log`

No GPU / WSL / Gemini needed — pure DB + file inspection. Safe to re-run; reads only.

Usage:
  python scratch/verify_highlights.py
  python scratch/verify_highlights.py --videos-dir "G:\\My Drive\\Sharing\\Badminton\\Boxhill\\June 12 2026" \
      --highlights "G:\\My Drive\\Sharing\\Badminton\\Boxhill\\June 12 2026\\Highlights"
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import os
import re
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))

from backend.infrastructure.database import Database
from backend.utils.hashing import compute_video_id

_VIDEO_EXTS = (".mp4", ".MP4", ".mov", ".MOV", ".mkv", ".avi")
_DEFAULT_DIR = r"G:\My Drive\Sharing\Badminton\Boxhill\June 12 2026"


def _near_dup_pairs(segs, tol=1.5):
    """Count segment pairs whose start AND end are within `tol` seconds — the signature of a
    doubled rally. Also counts plain overlaps (start of one inside another)."""
    pairs = sorted((float(s["start_time"]), float(s["end_time"])) for s in segs)
    dups, overlaps = 0, 0
    for i in range(len(pairs)):
        for j in range(i + 1, len(pairs)):
            (s1, e1), (s2, e2) = pairs[i], pairs[j]
            if abs(s1 - s2) <= tol and abs(e1 - e2) <= tol:
                dups += 1
            elif s2 < e1:  # j starts before i ends → overlap (pairs sorted by start)
                overlaps += 1
    return dups, overlaps, pairs


def _reel_rally_count_from_log(out_dir, stem):
    log = os.path.join(out_dir, f"{stem} - run.log")
    if not os.path.exists(log):
        return None
    try:
        with open(log, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as fh:
            txt = fh.read()
    except OSError:
        return None
    m = re.findall(r"PUBLISHED reel:.*\((\d+) rallies\)", txt)
    return int(m[-1]) if m else None


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--videos-dir", default=_DEFAULT_DIR)
    ap.add_argument("--highlights", default=os.path.join(_DEFAULT_DIR, "Highlights"))
    ap.add_argument("--db", default=os.path.join("output", "sports_indexer.db"))
    args = ap.parse_args()

    db = Database(args.db)
    srcs = sorted(
        os.path.join(args.videos_dir, f) for f in os.listdir(args.videos_dir)
        if f.endswith(_VIDEO_EXTS) and os.path.isfile(os.path.join(args.videos_dir, f))
    )
    print(f"Verifying {len(srcs)} source videos against reels in:\n  {args.highlights}\n")
    all_clean = True
    for src in srcs:
        name = os.path.basename(src)
        stem = os.path.splitext(name)[0]
        vid = compute_video_id(src)
        segs = db.query_play_segments(vid, {})
        dups, overlaps, pairs = _near_dup_pairs(segs)
        reel = os.path.join(args.highlights, f"{stem} - Highlights.mp4")
        reel_mb = os.path.getsize(reel) / 1024 / 1024 if os.path.exists(reel) else None
        log_n = _reel_rally_count_from_log(args.highlights, stem)
        clean = dups == 0 and overlaps == 0 and reel_mb and reel_mb > 0
        all_clean &= bool(clean)
        flag = "OK " if clean else "!! "
        print(f"{flag}{name}")
        print(f"     video_id={vid}  DB_segments={len(segs)}  near_dup_pairs={dups}  overlap_pairs={overlaps}")
        print(f"     reel={'MISSING' if reel_mb is None else f'{reel_mb:.0f} MB'}  "
              f"log_rally_count={log_n}  run.log={'present' if log_n is not None else 'ABSENT'}")
        if dups or overlaps:
            print(f"     ⚠ NOT dedup-clean — {dups} near-dup + {overlaps} overlap pairs still in DB")
    print()
    print("RESULT:", "ALL REELS DEDUP-CLEAN ✅" if all_clean else "⚠ ISSUES ABOVE — investigate")
    sys.exit(0 if all_clean else 1)
